title: The kilogram is fixed by setting h to 6.62607015×10^−34 J s
summary: NIST defines the kilogram by fixing the Planck constant at 6.62607015×10^−34 joule-seconds. The 2022 CODATA row marks that same value exact.
body: NIST's kilogram page says the kilogram is defined by taking the fixed numerical value of the Planck constant h to be 6.62607015 × 10^{−34} when expressed in the unit J s, which the page equates to kg m^{2} s^{−1}, where the metre and the second are already defined. The BIPM table of defining constants prints h as 6.626 070 15 × 10^{−34} J s. The 2022 CODATA listing marks h exact. The digits are exact because the definition fixes them.
